 COMMON JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed these two cases U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02 . Since these two cases are arising out of one and same accident and cause of action are the same  (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3863/2022  c/w M.V.C.No.3864/2022 and the respondents are the same and to avoid multiplicity of proceedings and to avoid outcome of conflicting Judgments, these two cases are clubbed together.
M.V.C.No.3864/2022 clubbed with original M.V.C.No.3863/2022
and common evidence came to be recorded in the said case.
These two cases are proceeded for disposal by way of common Judgment.
03 . The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:

That on 01.08.2021 at about 04.30 p.m, the petitioner in M.V.C.No.3863/2022 was riding his Hero Honda Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-05-HQ-1300 along with petitioner in M.V.C.No.3864/2022 as pillion rider,
were proceeding near Jain Vidyaniketan School,
Jakkasandra Village, Kanakapura - Bengaluru National Highway, a Hero Honda Splendor Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-11-L-7330, driven by its rider, in a rash and negligent manner, came from behind and dashed against petitioner's Motor Cycle, due to which, both petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner in M.V.C.No.3863/2022 was shifted to Dr.Chandramma  (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3863/2022  c/w M.V.C.No.3864/2022 Dayananda Sagar hospital, Harohalli, wherein after first aid treatment he was shifted to KIMS hospital,
wherein he was admitted as inpatient and diagnosed Shivaram S Naik vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118821666/
2 for the injuries and has undergone surgery.

The petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical treatment, nourishment, attendant charges,
transportation etc., and he has to undergo further expenses towards removal of implants etc.,.
Prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 39 years and was working as Driver and was earning Rs.40,000/- p.m.
On account of accidental injuries, he has lost his source of income and unable to work as a driver and thus has suffered 100% loss of income.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner in M.V.C.No.3864/2022 was shifted to Dr.Chandramma Dayananda Sagar hospital, Harohalli, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and diagnosed for the injuries and has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical treatment, nourishment, attendant charges,
transportation etc., and he has to undergo further expenses towards medical treatment.

Prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and aged  (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.3863/2022  c/w M.V.C.No.3864/2022 about 47 years and is self employed and doing Real estate business and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m. On account of accidental injuries, he has lost his source of income and unable to do real estate business and thus has suffered 100% loss of income.
The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending Motor Cycle and in this regard the Harohalli Police have registered a case against rider of offending Motor Cycle.

The respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- and Rs.10,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 18% p.a.

On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed objections in both cases.

KA-11-L-7330 and the same is valid as on the date of accident and liability of this respondent is subject to  (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.3863/2022  c/w M.V.C.No.3864/2022

06. The respondent No.2 in his objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, income, occupation of the
c/w M.V.C.No.3864/2022 petitioners, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioners, treatment taken by the petitioners and expenses incurred by the petitioners and

admits that this respondent is the owner of offending Motor Cycle and the same was insured with respondent No.1 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident and respondent No.2 was having valid driving licence at the time of accident.

The accident did not took place due to his negligence and it is due to negligence of the rider/petitioner of the Motor Cycle and the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and hence pray for dismiss the petitions with costs against respondent No.2 in both cases.

14. So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has not produced any evidence or documents.

The petition filed by the petitioners in M.V.C. No.3863/2022 and M.V.C.No.3864/2022 U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 are partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner in M.V.C.No.3863/2022 is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,17,816/- (Rupees Six lakhs seventeen thousand eight hundred and sixteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The petitioner is at liberty to draw periodical interest.

The petitioner in M.V.C.No.3864/2022 is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,07,400/- (Rupees Four lakhs seven thousand and four hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future (SCCH-3) 29 M.V.C.No.3863/2022 c/w M.V.C.No.3864/2022 medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-)
from the date of petition till its realization.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details.

The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amounts with interest within two months from the date of these Judgments in both cases, with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending Motor Cycle.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- in each case.
